sentences.text:
1. The Petitioner who is a public servant working as Police Sub-Inspector, raises a challenge to the impugned order dated 24.07.2023 passed by the Maharashtra State Human Rights Commission (hereinafter referred to as "the Commission"), more particularly, the order recommending to pay Rs.1,00,000/- to the victim for violation of her human rights, to be recovered from the erring police officer (the Petitioner)
within a period of six weeks from the receipt of order.
2. The learned counsel Mr. Deshmukh, for the Petitioner submits that the Petitioner who is a Police Sub-Inspector was posted at Dadar Rushikesh 2/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt Police Station, Mumbai,
during 2019-2020.

During such time, the Respondent No. 4 victim filed a complaint against her husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law and brother-in-law, alleging offences punishable under Sections 498A, 354, 506 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code, 1908.
It is the allegation of her that,
although
the Petitioner was entrusted with the investigation of the case filed by her, she has not taken timely action and has delayed the investigation, thereby violating human rights

Feeling aggrieved by the delay caused in investigation, the grandfather of the Respondent No. 4 filed a Seema Amol Mulik vs The State Of Maharashtra (Through Its ... on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199701378/
1 complaint before the Maharashtra State Human Rights Commission, Mumbai, alleging that in spite of registering the offence on 07.03.2020, neither was the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure nor were the accused arrested, there was inordinate delay of 7 months and more in conducting the investigation, holding the petitioner responsible for the same.

sentences.text: It is alleged, that the police machinery has ignored the complaint filed by the Respondent No. 4.

As a result of which, in spite of registering an FIR on 07.03.2020 before the declaration of the national lock-down, the Petitioner has failed to record the statement of the Respondent victim under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and failed to issue notice to the accused persons under Section 41-A Rushikesh 3/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt of the Cr.P.C.
A grievance is made that, no charge-sheet was filed till filing of the complaint, before the Maharashtra State Human Rights Commission.
It is submitted that in pursuance of the complaint made by the grandfather of Respondent No. 4, the Commission issued notice to the Petitioner.
Upon being served, the Petitioner appeared before the Commission and filed her reply.

However, totally ignoring her defence taken in the reply the learned Member of the Commission has passed the order impugned recommending payment of compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- to the victim, to be recovered from the Petitioner, holding her responsible for the violation of human rights qua the Respondent No. 4.
3.

The learned counsel would submit that the Petitioner had brought to the notice of the Commission the situational facts and circumstances of the case in her reply to the notice issued by the Commission.

She has taken a stand that, though the offence was undoubtedly registered on 07.03.2020, but the recording of the statement of victim under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. could not take place, since the victim herself has expressed her difficulty to appear immediately before the Magistrate, to record her statement due to her aged father and grandfather.
It is also claimed by the Petitioner that, in fact the Respondent Rushikesh 4/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt No. 4 had assured that she would inform about her availability for recording of her statement.

It is her stand that apart from that particular offence, the Petitioner was also entrusted with investigation of other offences, as well as the security arrangement within the jurisdiction of Dadar Police Station.
No sooner the offence was registered, the COVID-19 pandemic started and nationwide lock-down was declared on 24.03.2020, which was extended from time to time.

During such time, the Petitioner was again assigned with the duties of security arrangement,
for maintenance of law and order, hence she was unable to investigate further in the matter.
The Petitioner had also availed Child Care Leave in the month of August 2020.

During her absence,
the investigation was transferred to one Mr. Naresh Patil, PSI, who recorded the statement of the victim and filed charge-sheet on 24.02.2021.
In the meanwhile, the Petitioner who had resumed her duty on 26.10.2020, was sent on deputation at Police Station, Kurla from December 2020.

It is pointed out by learned counsel that a Show Cause Notice dated 04.12.2022 was issued to the Petitioner for the delay caused in investigation of FIR filed by Respondent No. 4 to which the Petitioner has responded and explained the circumstances, and due to which, the investigation Seema Amol Mulik vs The State Of Maharashtra (Through Its ... on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199701378/
2 could not proceed.

sentences.text: It has been Rushikesh 5/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt categorically stated that, due to the COVID-19, the Court was not working, therefore, could not make any communication with the Court for recording statement of Respondent No. 4, and for the same reason, even the notices under Section 41A of the Cr.P.C. could not be issued to the accused.

After considering the response given by the Petitioner to the Show Cause Notice, her explanation has been accepted, and only penalty of strict warning was imposed upon her, vide order dated 10.01.2023.
4.

It is submitted that upon perusal of the relevant dates it would be evident that, after filing of FIR on 07.03.2020, there was a nationwide lock-down imposed, hence there was no opportunity to proceed with the investigation because of the prevailing circumstances.
During the lock-down itself the Petitioner had to proceed on Child Care Leave.
Hence, in the given circumstances, it is not appropriate to blame the Petitioner alone for the delay in the investigation of the crime.
The learned Member of the Commission has not at all taken into account the explanation offered by the Petitioner.

It is further submitted that the defence taken by the Petitioner was not disputed by Respondent No. 4, nor has the Respondent No. 4 demonstrated as to what prejudice is caused to the Respondent No. 4, due to the delay in investigation.

It is submitted that the Petitioner had served in Police Department for 7 Rushikesh 6/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt years and more, her past service is clean and unblemished, however, as a result of the impugned order, there would be a blot on her career.

It is further submitted that though the Commission has passed the impugned order, making recommendation to the State Government, the Additional Commissioner of Police, has accepted it and issued an order dated 27.09.2022, calling upon the Petitioner to deposit an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- within a period of six weeks, failing which, it would carry a penal interest of 12 % per annum, to be paid to the victim.

The Petitioner has, therefore, approached this Court immediately by filing the present Writ Petition and could secure the interim order on the condition of deposit of 50% of the amount in the Court and, accordingly, an amount of Rs.50,000/- has been deposited on 30.10.2020.
5.
We have heard the learned AGP who supports the impugned order, as well as Mr. Ohal, the learned counsel for the contesting Respondent No. 4.

Both the counsel unanimously submit that, the impugned order has been passed by the learned Member of the Commission, after affording opportunity of hearing to the Petitioner and applying the prevailing judicial precedents governing the field.
The Petitioner has been careless in handling that particular case, Rushikesh 7/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt hence the impugned order does not deserve any interference.
6. We have given a thoughtful consideration to the impugned order on the background of the documents placed on record.
We do not find anything unreasonable in the defence raised by the Petitioner for the delay caused in investigation of C.R. No. 86 of 2020, filed at the behest of Respondent No. 4.

The Petitioner has taken a categorical defence that Respondent No. 4, herself has not made a suitable date available for recording of her statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.,
which is not denied by her.

Although the learned Member of the Commission has recorded that, the pandemic cannot be made a ground or reason for not proceeding with the investigation when the Seema Amol Mulik vs The State Of Maharashtra (Through Its ... on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199701378/

This observation of the learned Member, according to us, is unconscionable for the reason that, the COVID-19 patients were already detected in India in January 2020 and thereabout, even the World Health Organization ("WHO") has declared the outbreak of novel Coronavirus on 11.03.2020.
It was declared as a global pandemic, and stringent measures were directed to be taken for curbing the outspread of the pandemic.
The police machinery was brought into action for enforcement of the lock-down to restrict the outspread of the Coronavirus.
The police authorities being a part of law enforcement agency, were required to patrol the streets and Rushikesh 8/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt ensure the restrictions were scrupulously followed.
Thus, we are not in agreement with the findings recorded by the learned Member of the Commission, refusing to accept the explanation for the delay in the investigation.
According to us, in a densely populated city like Mumbai, restricting the movement of the people containing them to their houses was a great challenge before the law enforcement agency.

In normal circumstances, we certainly would have been in agreement with the views expressed by the learned Member of the Commission, but for the COVID-19 pandemic and the situation prevailing then, we do not agree.
The other glaring observation recorded by the learned Member is about the period during which the Petitioner has proceeded on maternity leave.
The Petitioner has proceeded on maternity leave in August, 2020, during which, the COVID-19 situation was still prevailing rather at its peak.

After she proceeded on leave, the officer, who was holding the charge in her place was also equally responsible for the investigation, which has been lost sight of by the learned Member, on the contrary, the learned Member has observed that, the Petitioner did not seek any direction from her senior to assign the investigation to other police officer, when in fact the other officer holding her charge was also responsible, yet no responsibility is fixed on him.
Rushikesh  9/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt 7.
It is true that usually there is lethargy and apathy on the part of the police officers to act on the complaints and investigate the offences registered by the citizens.
Once an offence is registered, the Investigating Officer is expected to act diligently and investigate the matter, so as to take it to its logical end, by following due procedure of law.

In the present case, it is observed by the learned Member of the Commission that there has been a delay of more than 7 months in the investigation,
and

only after the case was assigned to another police officer, the statement of Respondent No. 4 under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. came to be recorded on 11.12.2020, and thereafter the charge-sheet has been filed against the accused.
He has brushed aside the defence about outbreak of COVID - 19 Pandemic, in one line.

When in fact during those particular 7 months, the world was facing extremely difficult situation; the life of people was brought at stand still, therefore we are not in agreement with the observations made by the learned Member of the Commission that, delay in Seema Amol Mulik vs The State Of Maharashtra (Through Its ... on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199701378/
4 prompt investigation has resulted into miscarriage of justice to the victim and also violated her basic fundamental rights, as guaranteed under Article 21 and 14 of the Constitution of India.

sentences.text:
This observation is also not supported by any reasoning as to what prejudice is caused to Respondent No.
4, since the complainant as well as the accused all were confined to their respective houses,
Rushikesh 10/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt during the restrictions of the lock-down.
Even the case law relied upon by the learned Member of the Commission are all about the free and fair investigation and trials.
In the present case, there is no allegation about there being any unfair means adopted by the Petitioner.

The only grievance appears to be is the delay in investigation, which according to us,
was attributable to unprecedented situation prevailing due to COVID-19.
8. The learned Member of the Commission has miserably failed to appreciate the given circumstances, resulting in causing injustice to the Petitioner.
From the observation made in the impugned order, the approach of the learned Member of the Commission appears to be unreasonable, prejudiced and lopsided.
The learned Member has very casually brushed aside the explanation offered by the Petitioner, without giving it a second thought.
As a result, according to us, the impugned order becomes unsustainable, to the extent it imposes penalty on the Petitioner.
Even the penal order of recovering the compensation granted in favour of the victim to be paid by the Petitioner, is not supported by a reason as to why the victim needs to be compensated.
Since we have already held that, the delay itself was justifiable in the given circumstances, the penalty imposed also becomes unwarranted.

Hence, we set aside the impugned order only to the extent of Rushikesh 11/11 4 WP.13058.2023.odt clause (a), whereby an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is directed to be paid to victim Akshaya Kamble to be recovered from the present Petitioner.
So far as the rest of the order is concerned, we do not intend to interfere with the recommendations made by the learned Member.

As a result, the Writ Petition is partly allowed by quashing and setting aside cause (a) of the impugned order dated 24.07.2023 passed by the learned Member of the Maharashtra State Human Rights Commission in MAS/Case No. 568/13/17/2021.
